newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish committee fixes coalition vote day.
newsitem.headline: Turkish committee fixes coalition vote day.

text.p: A Turkish parliamentary committee on Tuesday fixed a date later this month for a confidence vote in the anti-Islamist coalition of new Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz.
"The government confidence vote will be on July 12," speaker Mustafa Kalemli told reporters after a meeting of the parliament's advisory committee.
Deputies were expected to give final approval for the same date, requested by the government, at a vote later on Tuesday.
President Suleyman Demirel named conservative Yilmaz as prime minister on Monday in an attempt to deny power to the Islamists after months of political chaos.

Yilmaz, previously the main opposition leader, has been boosted by a wave of defections from a conservative faction allied to the Islam-based Welfare Party of outgoing Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan.
The new government, a minority coalition supported by a left-wing party, has around 12 more MPs on paper than its opponents in the 550-member national assembly.
Erbakan, Turkey's first Islamist leader, now heads the opposition in a loose alliance with former coalition partner Tansu Ciller's conservative True Path Party.
Speaker Kalemli said a list of the government's policies would be read out in parliament on July 7 and then debated on July 10 ahead of the vote.
Parliament should have begun its summer recess on Tuesday but the break has been indefinitely postponed because of the political uncertainty.
